svg.aria-label: A real lost segment, a SACK block reporting the data received after the gap, and the retransmission of just the missing piece

g.text: 210.7 ms: arrives with a gap before it
“I still need 5657, but I have 5828 to 6418”

ol.li: The server sends three segments of the web page. The middle one, bytes 5657 to 5828, is lost somewhere on the way.
The next one arrives with a gap in front of it. The Pi can’t hand its bytes to the program yet (TCP delivers a stream in order), so it keeps them, and waits.
The Pi’s acknowledgement still says 5657, the first byte it’s missing, as Chapter 13’s cumulative ACKs did. But it adds a SACK block, a selective acknowledgement: “and I also have 5828 to 6418”.
So the server knows exactly what’s missing, and resends only that: 171 bytes, instead of everything after the gap (Chapter 13’s “go back N”).
The hole is filled. The Pi hands all of it to the browser, and acknowledges everything up to 6418 in one go. The whole repair took 90 milliseconds.

figure.figcaption: A real loss, repaired with a selective acknowledgement.
